the upper body is more highly correlated with waist circumference and the lower body is more highly related to the thigh circumference.
upper-body obesity is characterized by a high waist-to-hip circumference ratio (WHR), while lower-body obesity is characterized primarily by a high thigh circumference.
the upper body fatness component is best measured by the waist circumference and the lower body fatness component by the iliac crest or the thigh circumference.

the development of an objective method to describe body fat distribution.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
upper and lower body fat patterning in adult women is best characterized by the circumferential measurement of the waist, thigh, and iliac crest.

the fat patterning found in obese women is not consistent with the traditional concept of android or gynoid fat patterning, nor does it correspond to the concept of central versus peripheral fat patterning.

fat patterning in the obese woman is characterized by a large amount of subcutaneous fat distributed primarily in the upper body, with the greatest accumulation being in the waist and the second greatest in the thighs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trunk is a better predictor of upper than of lower-body fatness.

the trunk is more important than the extremities for upper-body fat pattering, that the thigh is more important than iliac crest for lower-body fat patterning, and that arm circumference does not contribute significantly to fat patterning in either upper or lower body.
the trunk is a major site of fat deposition in the obese, and the upper and lower extremities and the lower abdomen are relatively spared.
The main takeaway from our work is that
upper-lower fat distribution is more important than trunk-extremity patterning for the prediction of body composition.
the waist circumference is a good predictor of upper-body obesity and that thigh circumference is the best predictor of lower-body obesity.
the waist circumference should be considered the best single predictor of fat distribution.
